main_content.text: Our Work, Real Case Studies and a Downloadable Digital Marketing Portfolio PDF
Websites, apps, campaigns and brands we have built, shown with client permission and numbers you can check.

A digital marketing agency portfolio is a collection of real projects that shows what an agency did, for whom and what changed as a result. This page is Afwan Tech's portfolio. Every case study follows the same structure: the starting point, the solution, the work we did, results measured from the client's own data and the client's permission to publish. You can also request our digital marketing portfolio PDF to read offline or share with your team.

We hold our case studies to a simple rule: if we cannot show where a number came from, it does not appear. That means you will not find invented revenue figures, stock-photo testimonials or logos of companies we have not worked with. Some of our work is covered by confidentiality agreements, so it appears in anonymised form or not at all. What is here is meant to help you judge how we think, how we work and whether we are a good fit for your project.

items: Case studies across websites, apps, custom software, e-commerce, SEO, paid ads, social media and branding
Results shown with their source, time period and starting point
Client names, logos and quotes used only with written permission
A downloadable digital marketing portfolio PDF, available on request
References from past clients available for serious enquiries

main_content.text: How to Read Our Case Studies
Every case study on this page, and in our digital marketing portfolio PDF, uses the same layout. That makes it easy to compare projects and to see exactly what we were responsible for.

rows: Who the client is (or an anonymised description), their sector and size
The situation before we started, with baseline numbers where available
What the client wanted to achieve, in their words
The approach we chose and why, including what we decided not to do
The specific deliverables: pages built, campaigns run, features shipped
How long the work took, from start to the results reported
Measured outcomes, with the data source and time period stated
What worked, what did not and what we would do differently
A quote from the client, published with permission

main_content.text: Where a section does not apply, for example when a business has no reliable baseline data, we say so instead of leaving a gap. We include the "what we learned" section on purpose. Real projects rarely go perfectly, and an honest account of what fell short is often more useful to a future client than a list of wins.
Marketing Case Studies With Solutions, Organised by Service

Many people looking for marketing case studies with solutions want to see the problem and the fix side by side, not just a headline number. Our case studies are grouped by the service involved, and each one names the measures that matter for that kind of work.

rows: Slow, outdated or hard-to-edit site that does not bring enquiries
Page speed and Core Web Vitals, enquiry conversion, editing time for the client's team
Manual processes in spreadsheets and chat groups
Time saved per task, errors reduced, adoption by staff
Store that is slow, hard to manage or losing sales at checkout
Conversion rate, checkout completion, average order value, page speed
App idea or existing app with low usage
Active users, retention, crash-free sessions, store ratings from real users
Organic clicks and impressions, enquiries from organic search, indexed pages
High cost per lead or unclear return
Cost per lead, lead quality, cost per sale, return on ad spend
Inconsistent posting, little engagement, no enquiries
Engagement quality, profile actions, enquiries and sales from social
Task completion, user feedback, consistency across channels

main_content.text: What Our Work Looks Like, Service by Service
Beyond headline results, it helps to know what we actually deliver in each type of project. This is what you will see documented in the full write-ups.
Websites

Website projects show the sitemap and content plan, key page designs on mobile and desktop, the platform chosen and why, speed and Core Web Vitals before and after, redirect plans for redesigns, and how the owner's team now edits pages. Where enquiries are tracked, we show how form, call and WhatsApp conversions changed after launch.
Custom Software and Portals

For web applications and portals, we show the process before and after, the main screens with sensitive data hidden, the integrations built and how many people use the tool. The most meaningful results here are often time saved, fewer errors and staff who stopped using spreadsheets, rather than traffic.
Online Stores

Store projects show the platform, catalogue structure, product page templates, checkout and payment set-up, shipping integrations and speed work. Results usually cover conversion rate, checkout completion, average order value and the share of sales coming from mobile.
Mobile Apps

App write-ups show user journeys, key screens, the technology chosen, the admin panel and store listings. We report measures such as active users, retention after the first weeks, crash-free sessions and themes from genuine store reviews.
SEO

SEO projects show the audit findings, technical fixes, pages improved or created and the local work done. Results are taken from Search Console and analytics: clicks, impressions, enquiries from organic search and pages ranking for priority terms, always with dates.
Paid Ads

Paid campaigns show account structure, targeting, creative examples, landing pages and tracking set-up. We report spend, leads, cost per lead, lead quality from the sales team and, where tracked, cost per sale or return on ad spend.
Social Media

Social projects show the content plan, examples of posts and short videos, community-handling rules and reporting. Results focus on engagement quality, profile actions and enquiries or sales that can be traced to social channels.
Branding and Interfaces

Branding and interface projects show research findings, concepts, the chosen direction, guidelines or design systems and the identity applied to real materials. Where interfaces were tested, we show what users struggled with and how the final design changed.
How Do We Measure Results Fairly?
Numbers in a portfolio are only useful if they are fair. These are the rules we follow when writing up results:

items: Baseline first: we state what the numbers were before our work started, over a comparable period.
Same period comparisons: seasonal businesses are compared year on year, not month on month.
Clear attribution: when several things changed at once, such as a new website and a price cut, we say so and do not claim the whole effect.
Source named: each figure is tied to the tool it came from, such as analytics, Search Console, an ad platform, a store dashboard or the CRM.
Ranges when needed: if a client prefers not to share exact figures, we use ranges or percentages and say that we have done so.
No cherry-picking: we do not publish a single good week as if it were a lasting result.

main_content.text: Featured Case Studies

Note: Case study cards are placed here only from real, client-approved projects that follow the structure above (see the implementation notes in Part 6). Each card shows the client or anonymised description, service, industry, timeline, one or two verified results with their source, and a link to the full case study.

Our featured work is chosen to show range rather than only the largest numbers. You will see small local businesses next to growing brands, and projects where the main result was time saved or a smoother process, not only traffic or revenue. If you are looking for work in a specific industry or service that is not shown here, ask us; we may be able to share an anonymised summary or arrange a reference call.
What a Full Case Study Includes

Each full case study page goes beyond the card. It typically shows before-and-after screenshots, the key decisions made during the project, a short timeline, the measured results with their source, the team members involved and, where the client agrees, a quote or short video. Where the client's data is confidential, we describe results as ranges or percentages and say so clearly.
How Do We Choose Which Projects to Feature?
A portfolio is a selection, so it is fair to ask how the selection is made. We feature projects that:

items: Have stable, measured outcomes rather than early or one-off spikes.
Show a range of business sizes, industries and services.
Illustrate a clear decision, such as choosing to repair rather than rebuild, or to start with organic search instead of ads.
Have written approval from the business owner for everything shown.
Remain accurate today; older projects are updated or retired when details change.

main_content.text: We do not feature only our largest or most flattering projects, because a small business owner learns more from a project like theirs than from a headline figure that does not apply to them.
What Does a Good Result Look Like?

"Good" depends on where a business starts. A modest change can be a big win for a small company, while a large company may measure success in efficiency rather than growth. This table shows the kind of outcomes we consider meaningful at different stages.

rows: More calls, messages and bookings; a site the owner can update
First paying users, retention after the first weeks, lower cost to acquire users
Higher conversion and order value, lower ad cost per sale, faster pages
Time saved, fewer errors, better adoption of internal tools, steady organic growth
Easier tasks for users, consistent identity, fewer support questions

Why We Do Not Put Everything in One Public PDF

Some case studies include details that clients are happy to share privately but not publicly, such as revenue ranges or internal tools. For those, we may send a tailored version of the digital marketing portfolio PDF to a specific enquiry, with the client's permission, rather than publishing it to everyone.
How Do You Judge Any Digital Marketing Agency Portfolio?
Every agency portfolio looks impressive at first glance. These checks help you separate real evidence from decoration, whether you are looking at our work or anyone else's.

items: Are clients named, or at least described specifically enough to be believable?
Do results include a starting point, a time period and a data source?
Are screenshots and photos of the actual work, or generic stock images?
Are testimonials attributed to real people you could contact, with permission?
Do the numbers look suspiciously round or uniform across very different projects?
Is it clear what the agency did, as opposed to what the client or other vendors did?
Does the agency mention any project that did not go to plan, and what it learned?
Will the agency put you in touch with a past client for a reference call?

main_content.text: A digital marketing agency portfolio that passes these checks tells you far more than one with larger but unexplained numbers.
Warning Signs in a Portfolio

items: Results described as "verified" with no source or date.
The same photo used for different named people across a website.
Client logos shown without any case study or reference behind them.
Very large figures, such as total revenue generated for all clients, with no explanation of how they were calculated.
Testimonials with full names but no company, role or way to confirm them.

main_content.text: Why Are Honest Case Studies Important in India?

Beyond being good practice, honesty in case studies and testimonials is expected under Indian consumer rules. The Central Consumer Protection Authority's Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements and Endorsements, notified on 9 June 2022, say that claims about objectively verifiable facts should be capable of substantiation, and that endorsements should reflect the endorser's genuine and reasonably current opinion. The Bureau of Indian Standards published IS 19000:2022 on online consumer reviews in November 2022, which says purchased reviews must be clearly labelled and that reviews written by people employed for that purpose should not be published.

For us, that means three simple rules. Every number in a case study can be backed by the client's data. Every quote comes from the client, with permission, and reflects their real opinion. And no review, rating or testimonial on our site is bought, written by our staff or invented.
Logos, Screenshots and Privacy

Screenshots make case studies credible, but they can also expose private information. Before anything is published, we remove or blur customer names, phone numbers, emails, order details and anything else that could identify a person, in line with India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and the business owner's own policies. Business logos appear only with written approval, and dashboards are cropped to show the relevant figures rather than whole accounts. If an owner later asks us to change or remove something, we do it promptly, on this page and in the PDF.
Our Approach Behind Every Project
The projects in this portfolio share the same way of working, which is often more useful to judge than any single result:

items: We start with an audit or discovery call, so the plan is based on facts rather than assumptions.
Every project has a written scope and an exact total before work starts.
Tracking and measurement are set up early, so results can be shown honestly later.
One team handles design, development and marketing, which reduces handoff problems.
Accounts, code, files and data stay in the owner's name throughout.
At the end, we hand over everything with clear notes and remain available for support if wanted.

main_content.text: Why Some of Our Projects Are Not Shown
Not every project can be public. Clients may have signed confidentiality agreements, may not want competitors to see their results, or may simply prefer privacy. In those cases we:

items: Leave the project out entirely, if the client prefers.
Publish an anonymised version that describes the industry and size without naming the client.
Share details privately with a prospective client, only with the original client's permission.
Never show logos, screenshots or quotes without written approval.

main_content.text: White-label work done for other agencies is never shown, because the end client did not hire us directly.
Questions to Ask Our Past Clients
When you speak to a reference, these questions will tell you more than any case study.

items: What was the situation before Afwan Tech started, and why did you choose them?
Did the team understand your business and ask the right questions?
Were deadlines, costs and scope clear and honoured?
How did they handle problems or changes during the project?
Did you receive all accounts, files and code at the end?
Would you hire them again, and for what kind of work?

main_content.text: Questions to Ask Your Own Team Before Reviewing Portfolios
Agree internally on what you are looking for, so portfolio reviews lead to a decision:

items: Which problem are we trying to solve, and how will we measure success?
Which industries or project types are most relevant to us?
Who needs to approve the choice of agency, and what evidence will they want?
What budget range and timeline are realistic for us?

main_content.text: Three Typical Situations Portfolio Visitors Are In
These situations are illustrative, not case studies. They describe common reasons people visit this page, with details changed.
Situation 1: A Marketing Manager Building a Shortlist

A marketing manager at a mid-sized manufacturer (details changed) has been asked to shortlist three agencies for a website rebuild and SEO. She needs evidence she can forward to her director. The most useful steps are to request the portfolio PDF, look for B2B or manufacturing examples, and ask for a reference call with a similar client.
Situation 2: A Founder Checking If We Can Build Their App

A startup founder (details changed) has a prototype and wants to know whether we have built similar apps. Rather than only reading case studies, the fastest route is a short call where we walk through relevant work, explain what we would do differently for their product and share an anonymised example if a public one does not exist.
Situation 3: A Student Looking for a Portfolio Example

A digital marketing student (details changed) searches for a digital marketing portfolio PDF to model their own job portfolio on. Our portfolio can show how case studies are structured, and the section below gives practical tips for building a personal portfolio.
Building Your Own Digital Marketing Portfolio PDF
Many people searching for a digital marketing portfolio PDF are building their own, for a job or freelance work. The same principles we use apply to an individual portfolio:

items: Use the case-study structure: starting point, goal, what you did, results, what you learned.
Show real work, even small or personal projects, rather than made-up client stories.
State where each number came from, such as Google Analytics, Search Console or an ad platform, and the time period.
Include screenshots of dashboards, ads or content you created, with sensitive data hidden.
Keep it short: four to six strong examples beat twenty weak ones.
Add certifications only if you actually hold them, with a link to verify.
Export the final document as a PDF with readable fonts and compressed images, and keep a web version too.

main_content.text: If you are early in your career and want to see how an agency structures its work, you are welcome to request our PDF as a reference.
How Long Should You Spend Reviewing Portfolios?

Choosing a partner is important, but reviewing portfolios endlessly rarely helps. A practical approach is to shortlist three providers, read two or three of each one's most relevant case studies, request their portfolio PDF or a short walkthrough, and speak to one reference each. That usually takes a week or two and gives far better evidence than browsing dozens of websites. Write down the same questions for every provider, so you compare like with like, and include the people who will approve the decision early.
Common Mistakes When Reading or Publishing Case Studies
These mistakes lead to poor agency choices or to case studies that hurt rather than help.

items: Choosing an agency because of one large headline figure without checking its source.
Ignoring the timeline, so results achieved over years are compared with promises made for months.
Treating client logos as proof of work, without asking what was actually done.
Publishing results without the client's written permission.
Rounding or inflating numbers to look more impressive.
Using stock photos for team members or clients.
Leaving out the starting point, so readers cannot judge the improvement.

main_content.text: What This Page Does Not Do
To keep this portfolio trustworthy, we do not:

items: Publish numbers we cannot back with the client's data.
Use stock photos to represent clients, team members or testimonials.
Show logos of companies we have not worked with directly.
Pay for, write or edit client reviews or testimonials.
Present illustrative examples as real case studies.
Share confidential client information without permission.

main_content.text: When Our Portfolio May Not Be the Right Guide
Our portfolio reflects the kind of work we do. It may be less useful if:

items: You need TV, radio, print or outdoor advertising, which we do not offer.
You need a very large enterprise platform with hundreds of integrations; ask us for a frank conversation about fit.
You need a specialist in a single platform we do not work with; we will say so and suggest looking elsewhere.

main_content.text: Special Cases and Edge Cases
Some projects need special handling when they appear in a portfolio.
Projects Built for Other Agencies
Some of our development work is done for other agencies under their brand. That work is never shown here, because the end client did not hire us directly and may not know who built it.
Projects Still in Progress
For ongoing work, we wait until results are stable before publishing. Early numbers can change quickly, and publishing too soon can mislead.
Results That Fell Short
Some projects do not hit their targets. Where the client agrees, we still publish what happened and what we learned, because it shows how we respond when things go wrong.
Regulated Industries
For healthcare, finance and education clients, case studies avoid health or financial claims and focus on process, design and technical work, with wording approved by the client's compliance team.
Multi-Vendor Projects
When several agencies worked on a project, we describe only our part and credit the others where the client agrees.
What Happens After You Review the Portfolio?

If something here looks relevant, the next step is a short discovery call. We ask about your goals, your current website or product, your timeline and budget range, then walk you through the most relevant examples in more detail, including any anonymised work we can share. If it makes sense, we propose a free audit of your website, store, app or accounts, followed by a written plan with the exact total. If our work is not the right fit, we will tell you, and where possible point you to the kind of specialist you need.
Making This Page and the PDF Accessible

We want everyone to be able to review our work. Screenshots on this page carry descriptive alternative text, case study text is real text rather than words inside images, and colours meet contrast guidelines. The PDF version uses tagged headings, readable fonts and compressed images, so it opens quickly on phones and works with screen readers. If you need the portfolio in another format, ask us and we will help.
Examples People Ask For Most Often
Some requests come up again and again when people review our work. If any of these match your needs, mention them when you contact us and we will prioritise the most relevant examples:

items: A business website rebuilt so the owner's team can edit it, with search rankings protected during the move.
A local business that started getting more calls after its profile, website and ads were fixed together.
An online store moved to a new platform without losing product pages from search results.
An internal tool that replaced spreadsheets for orders, stock or approvals.
A mobile app built with an admin panel, published under the owner's own store accounts.
A brand refresh carried across website, social media and printed materials.

main_content.text: Where a public write-up does not exist yet, we can walk you through the work on a call, showing only what the owner has agreed to share.
Working With Us From Anywhere

All the projects in this portfolio were run from our one office in Whitefield, Bengaluru, with many owners based in other cities and countries. Work happens through video calls, shared project boards, review links for designs and staging sites, and regular written updates. Owners in Bengaluru can meet us in person by appointment. We do not have branch offices elsewhere and do not describe any project as delivered from a local office we do not have.
Industries We Have Worked With

Our work spans small local businesses and growing companies in sectors such as professional services, healthcare and clinics, education and coaching, retail and e-commerce, manufacturing and distribution, real estate, hospitality and software. Specific industries appear in the case studies only where we have client permission to show them. If your industry is not listed, ask us; relevant experience is sometimes covered by confidentiality.
Why Trust This Portfolio?
We would rather earn trust through evidence than through badges. Here is what stands behind every case study in our digital marketing agency portfolio:

items: Numbers backed by the client's own data, with source and time period.
Written client permission for names, logos, screenshots and quotes.
Real screenshots and photos, never stock images.
Honest notes on what worked and what did not.
Reference calls with past clients for serious enquiries.
Consistent structure, so you can compare projects fairly.

main_content.text: Frequently Asked Questions About Our Portfolio
What is a digital marketing agency portfolio?
It is a collection of real projects showing what an agency did, for whom and with what measured result. A good one names its data sources and has client permission.
Can I download your digital marketing portfolio PDF?
Yes. Request it through the contact form, by phone or on WhatsApp, and we will email you the PDF with the same verified case studies shown on this page.
What information do you need to send the PDF?
Only your name, email and what you are interested in. We use them to send the PDF and follow up if you wish, and we delete them on request.
How do you verify the results in your case studies?
Results come from the client's own analytics, ad accounts, Search Console, store or CRM data, and we state the source and time period for each number.
Do your clients approve their case studies?
Yes. Every named client approves the case study, including names, logos, screenshots and quotes, in writing before it is published.
Why are some case studies anonymised?
Some clients have confidentiality agreements or prefer privacy. We then describe the industry and size without naming them, or leave the project out.
Are your testimonials real?
Yes. Every testimonial comes from a real client, in their own words, with permission. We never write, buy or edit reviews.
Do you include projects that did not go well?
Where the client agrees, yes. We include what we learned, because honest lessons are often more useful than only showing wins.
What are marketing case studies with solutions?
They are case studies that show the problem and the solution side by side: the starting point, what was done and the measured result, so readers can learn from the approach.
Can I speak to one of your past clients?
Yes, for serious enquiries. We arrange a reference call with a past client who has agreed to speak with prospective clients.
Do you have case studies in my industry?
Possibly. If none are shown, ask us; we may be able to share an anonymised summary or arrange a reference with the original client's permission.
Why do you not show client revenue figures?
Many clients keep revenue private. We show revenue only when the client approves, and otherwise report measures such as enquiries, conversion rates or time saved.
I am a student. Can I use your portfolio as a reference for my own?
Yes. Our case-study structure is a useful model, and this page includes tips for building your own digital marketing portfolio PDF with real, verifiable work.
Do you show white-label work done for other agencies?
No. Work done on behalf of other agencies is never shown, because the end client did not hire us directly.
How often is the portfolio updated?
We add new case studies when projects have stable, approved results, and we review existing ones so that the information stays accurate.
How do I start a project after reviewing your portfolio?
Call or WhatsApp 79798 50684, email contactafwantech@gmail.com or use the contact form. We start with a short discovery call and, for most services, a free audit.

bottom_content.text: Case Studies and a Digital Marketing Portfolio PDF Built on Evidence

**Afwan Tech** publishes its digital marketing agency portfolio with one simple rule: every number must be backed by the owner's own data, and every name, logo, screenshot and quote must be approved in writing. Our case studies cover website development, custom software, online stores, mobile apps, SEO, paid ads, social media and branding, and each one follows the same structure, from the starting point and goal to the work done, the measured results and what we learned along the way.

People looking for marketing case studies with solutions usually want to see the problem and the fix side by side. That is why every write-up states the situation before we started, the approach we chose and why, the specific deliverables and the outcome, with the data source and time period for each figure. Where a business prefers privacy, we publish an anonymised version or leave the project out.

If you prefer a document you can read offline or share with colleagues, request our digital marketing portfolio PDF. It contains the same verified case studies as this page, a short company overview, service summaries and our process, and we send it by email after a quick request through the contact form, a call or WhatsApp. We ask only for the details needed to send it.

Honesty in case studies is also expected under Indian consumer rules. The Central Consumer Protection Authority's 2022 guidelines on misleading advertisements expect claims to be capable of substantiation and endorsements to reflect genuine opinions, and the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 19000:2022 standard on online reviews says purchased reviews must be labelled. We go further: no review, rating or testimonial on our site is bought, written by our staff or invented, and no stock photo stands in for a real person.

When judging any portfolio, including ours, check for named or clearly described projects, results with a baseline and time period, real screenshots, contactable references and an honest account of what did not go to plan. For serious enquiries, we arrange reference calls with past owners who have agreed to speak with prospective partners.

We choose which projects to feature for range, not only size. You will find small local businesses next to growing brands, and projects where the main win was time saved or a smoother process rather than traffic. Each case study is reviewed regularly and retired when details are no longer accurate. Screenshots are cropped and blurred so that no customer's personal data is ever exposed, and owners can ask us to change or remove anything at any time, on the page and in the PDF version of this digital marketing portfolio.
Students and job seekers building their own portfolio can use the same structure: real work, clear sources for every number, short write-ups and a compact PDF with a web version alongside it.

After reviewing our work, the next step is a short discovery call where we walk through the most relevant examples and, for most services, offer a free audit. mainEntity.name: What is a digital marketing agency portfolio?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is a collection of real projects showing what an agency did, for whom and with what measured result. A good one names its data sources and has client permission.

mainEntity.name: Can I download your digital marketing portfolio PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Request it through the contact form, by phone or on WhatsApp, and we will email you the PDF with the same verified case studies shown on this page.

mainEntity.name: What information do you need to send the PDF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only your name, email and what you are interested in. We use them to send the PDF and follow up if you wish, and we delete them on request.

mainEntity.name: How do you verify the results in your case studies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Results come from the client's own analytics, ad accounts, Search Console, store or CRM data, and we state the source and time period for each number.

mainEntity.name: Do your clients approve their case studies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Every named client approves the case study, including names, logos, screenshots and quotes, in writing before it is published.

mainEntity.name: Why are some case studies anonymised?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some clients have confidentiality agreements or prefer privacy. We then describe the industry and size without naming them, or leave the project out.
Yes. Every testimonial comes from a real client, in their own words, with permission. We never write, buy or edit reviews.

mainEntity.name: Do you include projects that did not go well?

acceptedAnswer.text: Where the client agrees, yes. We include what we learned, because honest lessons are often more useful than only showing wins.

mainEntity.name: What are marketing case studies with solutions?

acceptedAnswer.text: They are case studies that show the problem and the solution side by side: the starting point, what was done and the measured result, so readers can learn from the approach.

mainEntity.name: Can I speak to one of your past clients?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for serious enquiries. We arrange a reference call with a past client who has agreed to speak with prospective clients.

mainEntity.name: Do you have case studies in my industry?

acceptedAnswer.text: Possibly. If none are shown, ask us; we may be able to share an anonymised summary or arrange a reference with the original client's permission.

mainEntity.name: Why do you not show client revenue figures?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many clients keep revenue private. We show revenue only when the client approves, and otherwise report measures such as enquiries, conversion rates or time saved.

mainEntity.name: I am a student. Can I use your portfolio as a reference for my own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Our case-study structure is a useful model, and this page includes tips for building your own digital marketing portfolio PDF with real, verifiable work.

mainEntity.name: Do you show white-label work done for other agencies?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Work done on behalf of other agencies is never shown, because the end client did not hire us directly.

mainEntity.name: How often is the portfolio updated?

acceptedAnswer.text: We add new case studies when projects have stable, approved results, and we review existing ones so that the information stays accurate.
